results.title: IETF RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics
results.snippet:
### Description

The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is a stateless application-level protocol for distributed, collaborative, hypertext information systems. This document describes the overall architecture of HTTP, establishes common terminology, and defines aspects of the protocol that are shared by all versions. In this definition are core protocol elements, extensibility mechanisms, and the "http" and "https" Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) schemes.

results.title: 📄 HTTP Documentation
results.snippet:
# 📄 HTTP Documentation

HTTP is defined by these IETF RFCs and IANA registries.

## Core Specifications

The “core” semantics of the HTTP protocol are defined by:

 RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
 RFC 9111: HTTP Caching

Those semantics are expressed “on the wire” in three ways:

 RFC 9112: HTTP/1.1
 RFC 9113: HTTP/2
 RFC 9114: HTTP/3

Later versions of HTTP offer field compression:

 RFC 7541: HPACK Header Compression for HTTP/2
 RFC 9204: QPACK Field Compression for HTTP/3 [...] RFC 5861: Cache-Control: stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error
 RFC 8246: Cache-Control: immutable
 RFC 9211: Cache-Status Header Field
 RFC 9213: Targeted Cache Control Fields
 RFC 9875: HTTP Cache Groups

### Content-Related Extensions

 RFC 6265: Cookies
 RFC 6266: Content-Disposition
 RFC 7694: Client Initiated Content-Encoding
 RFC 8144: Prefer Header Field
 RFC 8288: Web Linking
 RFC 8942: HTTP Client Hints
 RFC 9842: Compression Dictionary Transport [...] ### Connection and Intermediary Extensions

 RFC 7639: ALPN Header Field
 RFC 7838: Alternative Services
 RFC 8336: ORIGIN HTTP/2 Frame
 RFC 8441: Bootstrapping WebSockets with HTTP/2
 RFC 9209: Proxy-Status Field
 RFC 9218: Extensible Prioritization Scheme for HTTP
 RFC 9220: Bootstrapping WebSockets with HTTP/3
 RFC 9298: Proxying UDP in HTTP
 RFC 9412: Origin HTTP/3 Frame
